title: E1.S NVMe device LED is blinking abnormally.
rootcause:

2. Refer to the attachment to enable VMD. After enabling VMD, Hotplug, RST, Error, and LED are all taken over by VMD.

title: Forced shutdown can cause abnormal vGPIO behavior in the system.
rootcause:
Root cause of the CPLD failing to update the vGPIO status under this specific stress sequence involves a race condition, priority conflict, and state-machine desynchronization between the BMC and the CPLD:
1. BMC-Induced I2C/SMBus Arbitration Lock (Bus Congestion).
2. State Machine Race Condition & Asynchronous Reset Timing.
3. PFR (Platform Firmware Resilience) or ERoT / Security Handshake Overhead.
description:

steps:
1. Power on the system to Shell.
2. Type "exit" to enter the BIOS setup menu.
3. Modify the BIOS settings and choose Save & Exit.
4. Verify whether the BIOS settings have been saved or not.
title: Setup menu data can't be saved when the system into the BIOS setup menu from Shell.
rootcause:
The SetupReentryHook is called after PostManagerHandshake(), before entering Setup. 
It is also called when returning to Setup after a Boot Override operation.
This hook is primarily used to handle the Setup re-entry flow and can be utilized to disable NVRAM write protection (such as the NVLock mechanism).
The bundled AMISetupNVLock module version is 13 or above, which has already fixed the issue of being unable to save setup settings after executing exit from the internal Shell to enter the BIOS Setup menu.
description: There is a 50% chance that the setup menu data can't be saved when the system into the BIOS setup menu from Shell.

title: Overriding the root port's PCIe device settings by project.sdl will cause a build error.
rootcause:
Previously, it was possible to directly override the root port's PCIDEVICE settings in project.sdl.
However, in recent AptioV versions (especially on newer platforms or with the latest BIOS build tools), the structural checks for the PCI hierarchy have become stricter.
** Copy the PCIe device that needs to be overridden to project.sdl, set disable=Yes, and then re-declare the same settings in the same project.sdl. This should allow the build to pass and resolve the failure.
description: Overriding the root port's PCIe device settings by project.sdl will cause a build error.

title: POST Hang at Checkpoint 0x26, 0x01 with Faulty DIMM or Unsupported DIMM Population.
rootcause: Faulty DIMM or Unsupported DIMM Population configs.
description:
According to current data, we believe Promote Warnings = Enabled would caused system hang at memory training.
Promotion knobs (Promote Warnings and MRC Promote Warnings) enabled, BIOS will not disable the DIMMs on the channel and continue booting and will consider the failure as a fatal error then hang the system.
If bad part still installed and both promotion knobs are disabled, EWL Major Code = 0x26, Minor Code = 0x1 will still occur (failure is still consistence) but system will go through disabled channel flow and drop to F-config to boot continuously.
If you get the opposite result, please feel free to share us higher debug level serial log to analyze further.
